name: Malta
title: Holidays in Malta
intro: Sunny, English-speaking islands with clear water, old forts and Popeye's village. Here's what Malta is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.

facts.label: Plugs
facts.value: Type G · same as the UK

facts_note: Malta drives on the left, like the UK. The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April to June and September to October are the sweet spot, warm with a calm sea. July and August are hot and busy. Winter is mild and sunny enough for sightseeing, though too cool for most to swim.

things.name: Valletta
things.blurb: A tiny walled capital. Watch the noon cannon fire at the Saluting Battery.

things.name: Popeye Village
things.blurb: The film set from the 1980 movie, now a colourful play village by the sea.

things.name: Blue Lagoon, Comino
things.blurb: Bright turquoise water a boat ride away. Go early or late to avoid crowds.

things.name: Blue Grotto
things.blurb: A small boat trip into sea caves that glow blue.

things.name: Mdina
things.blurb: A silent walled city on a hill, with honey-coloured streets.

things.name: Golden Bay
things.blurb: One of Malta's few big sandy beaches, with shallow water.

faqs.question: Is Malta good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's small, safe and easy, English is an official language, and the flight is about three hours. Many beaches are rocky, so pack water shoes.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: A week covers Malta's sights, beach days and a trip to Gozo or Comino.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for up to 90 days in any 180 without a visa. New EU entry checks are being brought in, so check GOV.UK before you travel.

faqs.question: Malta or Gozo?
faqs.answer: Malta has more hotels, sights and buses. Gozo is quieter and greener, and only a 25-minute ferry away, so many families stay on Malta and day-trip to Gozo.
